why_a_file_and_not_a_count: A count is a cached derivation and this project has watched one rot three times (PROTOCOL rule 13). Each entry carries the `kind` and the `note` that make the citation honest, which is the half of the fix that would otherwise live in 43 files of prose.
read_this_first: 57 of these 66 entries are NOT broken references: `destination` 25 (the citing script CREATES the path), `regenerable` 15 (constraint 6 working -- keep the generator, delete the artefact), `negative` 7 (the sentence says the path is wrong), `promoted` 4, `transient` 3, `quote`/`example`/`generated-record` 1 each. Only `lost` 9 are gone for good, and each of those notes says what the artefact showed and where the surviving evidence for it is. Counts as of TASK_125; re-derive with `harness/tools/temp_citations.py`, which prints the histogram.

kinds.example: an illustrative path in a usage line, never a real one
kinds.generated-record: the string is inside a GENERATED artefact; not a citation
kinds.lost: gone and not regenerable; the note says what it showed
